full_judgment:
"Let a Rule be issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 8-6-2014 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Brahmanbaria in Criminal Revision No. 84 of 2014 allowing the Criminal revision in modifying the order dated 4-6-2014 passed by the learned Senior Judicial Magistrate, Brahmanbaria in Petition Case No. 12 of 2014 directing the Officer-in-Charge, Nabinagar Police Station, Brahmanbaria to take lawful action after holding investigation of the allegation in the body of the complaint should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 The petitioner as complainant, on 1-6-2014 filed a Complaint Petition No. 12 of 2014 before the Court of Senior Judicial Magistrate, Nabinagar, Brahmanbari a alleging that on 29-4-2014, Tuesday at 12.30 PM, 3 (three) persons in civil dress entered into the house of Samsul Hoque, the uncle of complainant, asked about the sons of Rahis Mia and Samsul Hoque who disclosed that Shahnur Alam alias Shahinur (now dead) is at house. The three persons asked Shahnoor for water and in the meantime, unknown 9 (nine) persons in civil dress entered into rooms, hurriedly wore their dress and caught hold of the Shanoorand at gun point took away, on that day at Magrib brought him to Bhoirob RAB Camp. On 29-4-2014 at 11.00 pm to 1.30 pm at night Bhoirob RAB Camp captain Major AZM Sakib Siddique seriously wounded him upon beating mercilessly in different parts of his body. Thereafter Shahnoor became senseless and regained at 8.30 of morning and on 30-4-2014 Shahnoor was brought to Nabinagar Police Station. Accused No. 3 Md. Abu Taher being informant lodged Nabinagar Police Station Case No. 82 dated 30-4-2014 against Shahnoor and others and showing his arrest on 1-5-2014 was produced before court and before filing of case S.I. Enamul Hoque Bhuiyan on 29-4-2014 prepared a seizure list of the case. Due to deteriorating of health condition of Shahnoor on 4-5-2014 the Brahmanbaria Jail authority sent him to Brahmanbaria Sadar Hospital and on the same day he was admitted to Comilla Medical college Hospital and on 6-5-2014 at 5.30 hours Shahnoor died and on 7-5-2014 the unnatural death case No. 03/21 was lodged with Comilla kotwali Police Station. Due to torture of RAB the death of Shahnoor was caused and hence the petition of complaint. 

 3. The learned Magistrate after examining complainant upon oath under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on 1-6-2014 fixed the next date of the case on 4-6-2014 for further hearing and order. On 4-6-2014 the learned Magistrate after hearing passed an order and sent the petition of complaint to the Officer-in-Charge, Nabinagar Police Station, Brammanbaria with a direction to record the same as First Information Report (FIR) and to hand over the case to CID for holding investigation and report fixing the next date on 4-8-2014 for police report. 

 5. The informant being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid order dated 8-6-2014 preferred this Criminal Miscellaneous Case before this Curt under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained this Rule. 

 6. Mr. Ashrafur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the complainant-petitioner very outset submits that the learned Magistrate after examining the Complainant upon oath directed the officer-in-change to treat the petition of complaint as First Information Report (FIR) and to hold investigation, so there is nothing wrong in the procedure under section 156(3) and 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He further submits that since the court of law directed the concerned police station to treat the petition of complaint as First Information Report (FIR) in a case which is involved with murder as a schedule cognizable offence, the accused has to surrender before the court of law before filing revisional application in the Court of sessions, Since the accused has not surrendered in the court, so he is fugitive from the court of law. He further submits that in exercising the power under section 439A read with section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the accused has to obtain bail from the court of law or he has to go in jail custody but without exhausting the process of law, the accused filed criminal revision and the learned sessions Judge exceeded his power in revisional jurisdiction and modified the order of the learned Magistrate. The accused cannot get redress from any court of law without surrendering in court. So he prayed for making the Rule absolute for the ends of justice. The learned Advocate cited the case of Yakub Ali vs State. 47 DLR (AD) 94. 

 9. It appears from the records that the complainant filed a petition of complaint on 1-6-2014 against 4 (four) accused persons named in the petition of complaint and the complainant was duly examined upon oath as per law by the learned Magistrate on 1-6-2014, thereafter the case was fixed on 4-6-2014 for further hearing and order. The learned Magistrate after elaborate hearing on 4-6-2014 passed an order directing the officer-in-charge, Nabinagar Police Station, Brammanbaria to treat the petition of complaint as First Information Report (FIR) and also directed to investigate the case by CID. 

 12. The order passed by any court of law against any individual in a cognizable offence, the individual/the accused must surrender before the court of law to challenge the said order as a process of the court, but in the instant case, the accused Md. Enamul Haque has not surrendered before the court of law and as per law, he is fugitive from court. It is by now a well settled principle of law that an accused person who avoids the process of any court is a fugitive from justice and cannot seek justice without surrendering before the court of law. In this regard we may refer to the decision cited in the case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Mahmud Hossain, 61 DLR (AD) 17, wherein the Hon'ble Appellate Division observed as:— 

 "In the instant case, the accused Md. Enamul Haque having not surrendered to the process of the Court and could not file any application or put his grievance before a Court of law far less before the Sessions Judge. In the absence of any surrender before the process of law, the Court of law is incompetent to issue any order or stay any process at its behest and if done so that would be illegal and without jurisdiction." 

 13. In the facts of the instant case, it appears that the accused Md. Enamul Haque was neither in custody nor on bail when he filed the Criminal Revision and the sessions judge passed the order in revision as he was undoubtedly a fugitive from justice. The accused had not come before the court in a clean hand and the accused suppressed the facts of the case. 

 14. In the facts and circumstances, we are of the view that the accused Md. Enamul Haque was a fugitive from justice, so the subsequent order dated 8-6-2014 Passed by the learned sessions Judge is nullity under the law, since no court of law can give him any protection or entertain any application filed by him as fugitive. Moreover, the learned Magistrate has ample power to direct the officer-in-charge to treat the petition of complaint as First information report (FIR) and to hold investigation into cognizable case as per section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 15. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, the propositions of law cited and discussed above, and forgoing discussions, observations and reasons, we are led to hold the view that the learned Sessions judge passed the order on 8.6-2014 illegally and impropriety which should be quashed.
